tested_game: Steam 1.0.65 via isolated RE_Kenshi compatibility copies; original Steam 1.0.68 unchanged

actual_porthole.scope: Two anonymous private Porthole endpoints on one Windows PC, actual Steam transport, direct route. No two-PC WAN/NAT or forced Valve relay test.

udp_echo.scope: Actual Porthole3.0.2 anonymous Steam networking tunnel, same Windows machine; loopback-only UDP backend and remapped guest listener; not external WAN.

netlink_save.scope: Actual private Porthole anonymous local tunnel; real NetLink/ENet/SaveXfer; generated 3MiB host-to-guest save with bidirectional controls and entity motion; not independent WAN

link_metrics.scope: Two isolated anonymous Porthole processes on one Windows PC; no WAN claim

inventory.explanation: Normalized item type, quantity, nesting before and after core reload, both clients; equal across clients. No new shop UI or combat test in this release.

controlled_network_model.scope: Actual standalone NetLink/ENet/SaveXfer sender+receiver; generated saves; local relay model only, not actual Porthole or WAN

changes.profile: Opt-in KENSHICOOP_NETWORK_PROFILE=porthole, still ENet over UDP
changes.notes: MTU1200 is a conservative choice, not a Porthole hard limit. Queue bounds apply only to Porthole profile. Reliable bulk FIFO and channels retained. Slower initial world transfer is possible.

limitations: One-PC direct Steam route is not an independent WAN test.
No guarantee of lower Internet ping or FPS.
Actual native motion maximum observed gap on guest was 2844ms; controls max157/94ms.
Native 3MiB transfer tested host-to-guest only, with controls and motion both directions.
Long campaigns, arbitrary third-party mods, every shop/recruit variant and known RE_Kenshi focus error remain outside this test.
